fine_trace.note: The raw testcase is supplied to the OTS fuzzer as an sfnt font. Its table directory contains a Graphite Silf table at file offset 0x12a74 with length 0x16788.
The sfnt table map dispatches each supported table. The Silf table entry from the testcase is passed to Font::ParseTable with the original font bytes.

fine_trace.code: case OTS_TAG_SILF: table = new OpenTypeSILF(this, tag); break;
fine_trace.note: The Silf tag selects the Graphite SILF parser.
The testcase Silf table begins with version 0x00050001, so the parser takes the version 5 compressed-table path.
The testcase supplies compHead 0x0807c424. The high scheme bits select LZ4 and the low FULL_SIZE bits declare a 0x7c424-byte decompressed Silf payload.
The decompression destination is allocated for the attacker-controlled decompressed_size derived from compHead.
Compressed bytes following the Silf header are expanded into the temporary decompressed buffer using the declared 0x7c424-byte target size.
The parser recursively treats the LZ4 output as an uncompressed Silf table, preserving the attacker-controlled internal offsets and counts.
The decompressed Silf subtable offsets select a pass and provide next_pass_offset to the pass parser without validating that all derived pass sections are initialized input bytes.
Pass header fields from the testcase determine rcCode and aCode. Their difference controls how many constraint bytes will be consumed later.

fine_trace.code: unsigned long actions_len = this->oDebug ? this->oDebug - this->aCode :
fine_trace.note: The same pass offsets determine the action section length and subsequent parse position before later 16-bit fields are consumed.
The malformed decompressed pass reaches a 16-bit read in the pass parser. Under MSan, Buffer::ReadU16 reports use of uninitialized data from the expanded Silf payload.
ReadU16 copies two bytes from the current Silf buffer offset; the OSS-Fuzz crash state reports this function as the sanitizer sink.
